name: vibedev_rail_follow_up_context
content: - run_coding_task continues this task chain's coding session: the same engine resumes its own session, and a different engine (or a session that missed turns) gets Magician's handoff of the earlier turns; session_name, persist_session, and pi_binary overrides are rejected.
- If the parent produced a PLAN, read it in full first — it is the parent's plan.md output — and implement or refine it faithfully rather than re-planning from scratch.

- If the parent produced CODE, treat the real workspace as the source of truth but let run_coding_task inspect that state first; do not assume a prior proposal was applied unless the returned real_working_dir state shows it.
- Keep this an incremental follow-up. Prefer focused diffs over reworking unrelated areas, and stay inside the same VibeDev project.
- If the parent run still has unresolved code-review HITL, stop and ask for that review to be resolved before creating new changes.

metadata.description: Prose half of the `@vibedev` chat rail's follow-up continuation block. The machine-read `Parent task:` line of that block is assembled in Rust and deliberately NOT stored here: `execution/compiled_handlers/run_coding_task.rs` string-matches it back out to walk the run chain, and a prompt-store edit must not be able to break that contract silently. Mirrors the prose of the cockpit's client-side followUpContextBlock (ui/unified-ui/src/lib/shell/vibe/conversation/submit.ts) collapsed into one mode-agnostic block, because the rail selects a parent rather than being handed one and both parent kinds must read correctly.
metadata.author: magician
metadata.changelog: v1.1.0: Engine-neutral continuation wording — a follow-up on another engine starts a fresh session with Magician's handoff of earlier turns, so the prose no longer claims a shared session holds the parent's work. v1.0.0: Initial `@vibedev` rail follow-up continuation prose. Stage 1f: session/binary overrides are rejected, not optional.
